ASZF-052: Statutory warranty for defects, product warranty and guarantee
ASZF-054: In the event of defective performance, the consumer may assert a claim under the statutory warranty rules of the Civil Code and applicable consumer protection legislation. Subject to the conditions laid down by law, the consumer may choose to request repair or replacement, request a proportionate reduction in the price, have the defect repaired at the Seller’s expense, or withdraw from the contract. The consumer may not withdraw from the contract because of an insignificant defect. The consumer must notify the Seller of the defect without undue delay after discovering it. In a consumer contract, claims under the statutory warranty for defects are generally time-barred two years after performance; for second-hand products, the parties may agree to a shorter limitation period of at least one year.
ASZF-055: For consumer sales, any defect discovered within one year of delivery is presumed to have existed at the time of performance, unless this presumption is incompatible with the nature of the product or the defect. The Seller will record notifications of claims under the statutory warranty for defects in accordance with the requirements of law.
ASZF-057: If movable goods are defective, the consumer may, subject to the statutory conditions, request the manufacturer or distributor to repair or replace the product. A product warranty claim may be asserted within two years of the product being placed on the market by the manufacturer. The manufacturer may be exempt from liability if it proves one of the grounds specified by law.
ASZF-059: The Seller provides the mandatory guarantee required under the legislation in force for durable consumer goods, where the product and its purchase price fall within the scope of that legislation. The duration and detailed terms of the guarantee are set out in the guarantee certificate supplied with the product and in the applicable legislation. For products covered by the legislation, the current mandatory guarantee period depends on the purchase price: one year for products priced from HUF 10,000 up to HUF 100,000; two years for products priced above HUF 100,000 up to HUF 250,000; and three years for products priced above HUF 250,000. The absence of a guarantee certificate does not, by itself, affect the consumer’s rights under the guarantee; please retain proof of purchase.
ASZF-060: The consumer may have rights under the statutory warranty for defects, product warranty and guarantee concurrently; however, the consumer may not pursue overlapping claims for the same defect in a way that would result in double recovery. The detailed conditions of these rights are set out in Act V of 2013, Government Decree No. 373/2021 (VI. 30.) [Hungarian government decree], Government Decree No. 151/2003 (IX. 22.) [Hungarian government decree] and Decree No. 19/2014 (IV. 29.) of the Ministry for National Economy [Hungarian ministerial decree].
ASZF-061: Important limitation: consumer rights are available to natural persons acting as consumers. Different statutory provisions apply to customers purchasing as businesses. The Seller does not manufacture cash registers. Where a cash register is activated/set up for a Buyer, the Buyer is responsible for defects resulting from information provided incorrectly or incompletely by the Buyer, provided that the causal link can be established. This does not limit the Seller’s liability for its own defective performance or exclude any rights granted to consumers by law. The applicable rules for cash registers and related services must be determined on the basis of the relevant contract and the cause of the defect.

Where several products are delivered at different times, or a product consists of several lots or pieces, the period begins on the day the last product or lot is received. The consumer may exercise the right of withdrawal by sending an unequivocal statement before the withdrawal period expires. The statement may be sent to either of the following contact details: {EMAIL}; {ELADO}, {CIM}
ASZF-069: If the consumer withdraws from the contract, the Buyer must return or hand over the product to the Seller without undue delay and no later than 14 days after notifying the Seller of the withdrawal. The Buyer bears the direct cost of returning the product unless the Seller has agreed to bear that cost or the law provides otherwise. Within 14 days of becoming aware of the withdrawal, the Seller will refund the amount paid by the Buyer, including the cost of the least expensive standard delivery option; the Seller may withhold the refund until it has received the product or the Buyer has provided reliable evidence that it has been sent back. Unless otherwise agreed, the refund will be made using the same payment method as the original transaction.
ASZF-070: The consumer is liable for any diminished value of the product resulting from handling other than what is necessary to establish the nature, characteristics and functioning of the product. Statutory exceptions to the right of withdrawal — for example, performance of a service begun at the consumer’s express request, or a product made to the consumer’s specifications or clearly personalised — apply in accordance with Government Decree No. 45/2014 (II. 26.) [Hungarian government decree]. Whether an exception applies must be assessed individually for each product and service.
